label: Claude Fable 5.2
output:
Hi Mikaela, sorry it's taken me a few days. Yes we did, and here's the real version, bad bits and all.

The setup: 290 cows, mostly 3-way crossbreds. We started on 21 Sept, after mating had started. We skip the arvo milking on Tues, Thurs, Sat and Sunday, so four once-a-day days a week. Mornings are still 5.15 every day, that part doesn't change.

Production first since you asked. Milksolids are down about 6% on the same weeks last year, going off the Fonterra app. Our rep had told us to expect 8 to 10, so it's been better than we were warned.

Cells, yes they jumped. We went from 110k to about 180k in the first 3 weeks. They're back around 135k now, so still up on where we were but settled.

Now the bad one. We had a heifer with mastitis go bad on a skipped arvo. We didn't spot it till the next morning and she lost a quarter. You have to be on your game with teat spraying and checking cows on the skip days or it bites you. On a normal day you'd pick that up at the afternoon milking, and on a skip day nobody's had hands on her for 24 hours unless you make a point of going and looking. So don't think of the skipped arvos as fully off for whoever's in charge of the herd.

The good side. Lame cows are way down, 4 on the lame list now against 11 this time last year. Our long walk to the back paddocks is 1.8km, so cutting four of those return trips a week has made a real difference to their feet.

The cows came round quicker than I thought too. About 4 days of bellowing at the gate and then they were fine.

Staff wise, Kieran, our 2IC, said it's the first spring he hasn't wanted to quit by October. That might be worth mentioning to your young fella.

And the first Sunday arvo we skipped, Dave and I drove over to Hamilton to see the grandkids. First Sunday off in spring in 20 odd years.

Honestly, we wouldn't go back. The hours alone are worth the 6% to us. But that's us, and I don't want to talk you into it and have you cursing me in March. You'll take a hit on production, your cells will go up for a bit, and if you get slack on the skip days you can lose a quarter like we did. If Tom's knees are bad though, the arvos off will help him more than anything else you could change.

I'll have the shed rosters and our numbers with me at the Kerrisons on the 19th, so come and have a proper look. Grant, you're welcome to as well.

Or just ring me if you want, Mikaela. It's easier than texting and my thumbs are hopeless.
